solutions.check: 31 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Right way of going about beating up poor clot

indicators.note: something beaten up is knocked out of shape, so the letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneering remark that roughing up some hapless fool is the proper way to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for the clot, but both words are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the accepted code of correct procedure, the proper manner of conducting affairs or ceremonies.

clue.text: see 26dn.
Try to get off with Trilby, say, gaining access to part of bra

indicators.note: to gain access is to get inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a bra has two cups
a trilby is an example of a hat; 'say' flags the example

explanation.surface: A man called Trilby making a clumsy pass that ends with his hand inside someone's bra.
explanation.walkthrough: Trilby reads as a person's name, but it is the soft felt hat. The hat sits inside the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat someone up is to talk flirtatiously in hope of romance, an informal British idiom for trying to seduce.

clue.text: Snakes getting Dick to ensnare party leader

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
to ensnare is to trap and hold, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a dick and an ass are both slang for a fool
first letter of 'party'

explanation.surface: Political snakes recruit a man called Dick to trap the leader of their own party.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick looks like a name; it is slang for an idiot, as is ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous serpents of Egypt, the kind Cleopatra is said to have used.

clue.text: Massive entertainer's work stunt

blocks.note: a gig is a booking or performance for a musician or comic
an antic is a caper or prank

explanation.surface: A performer's huge stunt that has the audience gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Massive' looks like an adjective for the stunt, but it is the definition standing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size, so they are plain synonyms for huge.

clue.text: Balls examinations restricting energy

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: examinations are tests
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Medical examinations of the balls that sap a man's energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The E for energy goes inside TESTS, just before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Testes are the male reproductive glands, and balls is the everyday slang for them.

clue.text: Feel knackered again, so withdraw

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to tire is to feel exhausted; knackered is British slang for worn out

explanation.surface: Someone worn out once more decides to bow out and go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces backwards: 'again' supplies the prefix that comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw, whether from a job, from company, or to bed for the night.

clue.text: Start of Tories' downfall sequence

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of 'Tories'
rain is literally a fall from above

explanation.surface: A political commentator tracing the chain of events that began the Conservatives' collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' means political ruin in the surface but is read literally: a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of events or thought is a connected series, one thing following another in order.

clue.text: "He is cast out!" – whip

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, as in a bone put out, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A party whip announces a rebel MP has been expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' reads as one phrase meaning expelled, but 'cast' belongs to the letters and 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish, originally by beating, so it matches the verb to flog or lash.

clue.text: Press line on Washington upheaval, as exemplified by the storming of the Capitol

definitions.note: an example of the answer, introduced by 'as exemplified by'

indicators.note: a heave upwards lifts things, and in a down entry going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: to press around is to mob; a press is also a crowd
L is the abbreviation for line
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A newspaper's take on the turmoil in Washington when rioters stormed the Capitol in January 2021.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press line' looks like a newspaper's stance and 'Washington upheaval' like political turmoil; both are split into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob law is rule imposed by a lawless crowd, and the riot at the Capitol is a vivid instance of it.

clue.text: Ecstasy time at organised games

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to run an event is to organise it
games are sport

explanation.surface: Someone taking the drug Ecstasy during a school sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy with a capital looks like the drug, but it is the definition in its emotional sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport of joy is an overwhelming rapture, a literary sense of being carried away by emotion.

clue.text: Backing vehicles for Sting

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: trams are vehicles running on rails

explanation.surface: Backing vocals, or a backing vehicle, for the singer Sting.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the musician, but it is a verb here, and 'Backing' looks like musical support.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to feel a sharp stinging pain, as a cut does when antiseptic touches it.

clue.text: Restraint is quite OK when suppressing noisy Trump rebel leaders

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so each word gives only its opening letter
to suppress is to hold down and contain, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: cool is slang for fine or acceptable
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Holding back is acceptable when it means silencing loud rebels who back Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like the heads of the rebellion; it takes the initials of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Control and restraint both mean keeping something in check, holding back force or feeling.

clue.text: One squeezed into Dior creation (medium)

indicators.note: a creation is something newly made up, so the letters are fashioned into a new order
squeezed into means pushed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the fashion house name taken as letters
a means one

explanation.surface: A model squeezed into a tight Dior creation of medium size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creation' reads as a designer dress, and 'medium' as a dress size, but medium is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a medium of mass communication, alongside television and the press.

clue.text: One time to get into pain-in-the-arse exercises

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: piles, or haemorrhoids, are literally a pain in the backside
a means one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone finally finding time to take up a workout regime they find a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain-in-the-arse' looks like a complaint about the exercises, but it is read literally as an ailment of the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of controlled exercises for core strength and posture, named after its inventor.

clue.text: Genital area oil spread over two opposite directions

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
north and south are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: Massage oil being rubbed over the private parts in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The loins are the region of the hips and groin, often used as a euphemism for the sexual organs.

clue.text: Top disaster as a result of Coronavirus restrictions?

definitions.text: Top disaster as a result of Coronavirus restrictions?

blocks.note: surface reading: a catastrophe of the highest order

blocks.clueFragment: Top disaster as a result of Coronavirus restrictions?
blocks.note: setter's reading: 'top' is the head, so a mess made of the hair when barbers were closed during the pandemic

explanation.surface: The worst calamity caused by the pandemic rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as superlative, best or greatest, but means the top of the head; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: With salons shut in 2020, people cut their own or family members' hair, often with comic results.

clue.text: Could be messing with drug causes medical emergency

indicators.note: messing with something disturbs it, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A warning that dabbling in drugs might land you in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' reads as a hedge, but it supplies the letters; the drug adds one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Code blue is the hospital alarm called when a patient's heart or breathing stops and resuscitation is needed.

clue.text: It's designed to move a stiff male behind

definitions.text: It's designed to move a stiff

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
arse is British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A smutty reading about something built to shift a man's rigid rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse, so the definition is a vehicle for the dead, not anything ruder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin to the funeral, conveying the dead body.

clue.text: Grubby residue, result of poor diet, note

indicators.note: something poorly made comes out badly formed, so the letters emerge in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
to mark something is to note it

explanation.surface: A doctor's note that dirty build-up comes from eating badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor diet' looks like a cause of ill health; 'poor' is the anagram signal. A tidemark is the grimy ring left round a bath or on unwashed skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is a line of dirt left where water stood, as around a bath, a mainly British usage.

clue.text: Balls crushed by Bush in chamber

indicators.note: something crushed is squeezed tight on all sides, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: broom is a yellow-flowered shrub
Ed Balls is a British Labour politician, now a TV presenter

explanation.surface: Ed Balls being crushed by George W Bush in some legislative chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls and Bush both look like surnames, and one is: Ed Balls was a Labour minister, so Balls clues his first name. Bush is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamber is an old-fashioned word for a room, especially a private room where one sleeps.

clue.text: Infringement of Boris's first contact

indicators.note: first means the opening position, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of 'Boris'
to reach someone is to contact them

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's first social contact broke the pandemic rules, a nod to the partygate scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris's first contact' reads as one phrase; it splits into his initial and a verb for getting in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a violation of a rule or law, the same idea as an infringement.

clue.text: Jellyfish capable of making men rock hard?

definitions.text: capable of making men rock hard
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the Gorgon, not a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the free-swimming bell-shaped stage of a jellyfish

blocks.clueFragment: capable of making men rock hard
blocks.note: second meaning: the Gorgon of Greek myth, whose gaze turned men to stone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock hard' sounds like a smutty boast; read literally, it is men petrified into stone by a mythical monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological term for the bell-shaped jellyfish form borrows the Gorgon's name because its tentacles resemble her snake hair.

clue.text: Bonds a/c dodgy – scarper

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written; a/c is short for account

explanation.surface: A shady bonds account is uncovered, so the crook flees.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash in a/c is ignored; only the letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for running away, and to abscond is to flee secretly, usually from justice.

clue.text: Oxygen/iron treatment for a group of stars

indicators.note: a treatment processes material and changes it, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry process applying oxygen and iron, oddly prescribed for a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxygen gives its symbol; the treatment applies to both pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the constellation of the hunter, with his famous three-star belt, easily seen in winter skies.

clue.text: Bender results in bowel movement

indicators.note: movement means shifting position, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy drinking binge leads, unpleasantly, to a trip to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bender looks like a drinking session and 'bowel movement' like a bodily function; the elbow is a joint that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a bender is anything that bends, and the elbow is the joint that bends the arm.

clue.text: (& 28/2) Enthusiastically accompanied by Frank and members

blocks.note: with means in company of
frank here means candid or unconcealed, the opposite of closed
limbs, and limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly joined by a man named Frank and some club members.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name; it is the adjective for candid. Members is the old sense of limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone with open arms is an idiom for welcoming them warmly and eagerly.

clue.text: Perhaps Trump's attempted presidential role is embodied in "Nationwide spot is mine!"

indicators.note: to be embodied in something is to be contained within its body, so the letters sit inside a longer run

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word, the next two, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at Trump trying to claim the presidency as his own personal territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an opinionated example rather than a dictionary equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is absolute rule by one tyrant, and the setter casts Trump's bid to cling to office in that light.

clue.text: see 26dn.
Brenda's lot, quite comfortable lacking a quality of civility

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II; her lot is the royal court
easy means relaxed and at ease
taken as written; this is the letter removed

explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is a Private Eye joke name for the late Queen, so her lot is the court around her.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy is polite, considerate behaviour, the quality that makes a person civil to others.

clue.text: "Money!" the vocalist shouted

blocks.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A singer belting out a demand for cash, perhaps the song 'Money (That's What I Want)'.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
